adverse_media.summary: Adyen N.V. was a named defendant in Ericsson's patent action concerning EP 3397009. The reported settlement with the Verifone defendants also covered the claims against Adyen, and the court permitted withdrawal. The reviewed decision summary does not report an infringement judgment against Adyen.
adverse_media.status: Withdrawn following settlement covering the claims against Adyen; status checked as_of 2026-11-10.

adverse_media.category: Merchant litigation; alleged breach of duty
adverse_media.summary: Solitary B.V., as assignee of claims associated with bankrupt merchant Athlete.nl B.V., alleged that Adyen N.V. improperly increased reserves, delayed payment and obstructed a processor transition. Amsterdam District Court rejected the claims, accepting the objective basis for reserve calculations and finding that Adyen sufficiently considered the merchant's interests.
adverse_media.status: Claims dismissed at first instance. Subsequent appeal status not established as_of 2026-11-10.

adverse_media.summary: The Studygroup B.V. sued Adyen N.V. over termination of their Cousins-program collaboration, alleging a longer-term funding commitment. Amsterdam District Court rejected the alleged continuing commitment and dismissed the claims.
adverse_media.status: Claims dismissed at first instance. Subsequent appeal status not established as_of 2026-11-10.

adverse_media.summary: A judgment identifies Adyen N.V. as the victim of fraudulent SEPA direct-debit activity carried out through Moneybird accounts. Adyen brought recovery proceedings, and the court held defendants individually liable. This is operational fraud exposure, not a finding that Adyen perpetrated fraud.
adverse_media.status: Civil recovery judgments issued. Actual recovery and subsequent proceedings not established as_of 2026-11-10. The judgment text states May 8, 2024; the hosting page's metadata separately shows June 6, 2024.

adverse_media.summary: A former employee pursued Adyen N.V. over expiry and exercise conditions of employee options following resignation. Amsterdam Court of Appeal upheld dismissal of the claims, finding no relevant breach of employment duties or the option arrangement.
adverse_media.status: Dismissal upheld on appeal. Further proceedings not established as_of 2026-11-10.

excluded_findings.reason: The Trust & Verify patent case names Adyen Inc., not Adyen N.V.; excluded from this entity's adverse findings.
The DNB customer-due-diligence penalty concerns a different payment institution, not Adyen N.V.; excluded.

output.risk_rationale: Medium, provisional—not a completed sanctions clearance. The selected entity is the Dutch operating company Adyen N.V., independently identifiable in DNB's register. Leadership changes through the screening date have been incorporated. Reviewed company litigation was dismissed or withdrawn, while the SEPA case identifies Adyen as a fraud victim rather than a perpetrator. Historical state-enterprise board roles warrant former-PEP review, without establishing current PEP status. UK exact-name checks identified no full-name match, but OFAC and EU screening could not be completed. Direct KVK/GLEIF verification and current natural-person beneficial ownership also remain unresolved; the institutional notifications are not a substitute for UBO identification. These verification gaps require resolution before treating the company as cleared. ([dnb.nl](https://www.dnb.nl/en/public-register/information-detail?registerCode=WFTDG&relationNumber=F0001))
